$comment: src/shadow/run.ts's candidate set (zheref/nen#2, Akatsuki migration P1, the §7 shadow-window evidence bar). DATA, not code, for the same §3 reason every other repository name in this codebase lives in a schema file rather than a string literal: src/taxonomy-purity.test.ts sweeps every shipped .ts file for the name of a system nen serves, and a shadow-window target list is exactly that -- a list of systems nen is being pointed at, not a taxonomy nen decides with. Putting it in JSON keeps the sweep meaningful instead of teaching it a shadow-window exception.
closedOraclePrsComment: Issue #2's Scope: 'bankai-core's recently closed 907, 909, 911, 913, 916' -- named explicitly rather than discovered, because a closed PR's mergeable/checks/reviews state is a moving target only until it closes; these five are fixed points the evidence table can cite. NOTE: this object has no '$comment' KEY of its own (unlike the top level) -- src/shadow/run.ts iterates Object.entries() over it directly, and a stray string-valued key would be walked as a repo name.
knownReasonDivergenceComment: ../gates/ready.ts's header, ADOPTION DIVERGENCE (3): the oracle's empty-rollup message cites this issue by the source system's own name, which src/taxonomy-purity.test.ts forbids src/shadow/run.ts from carrying as a code literal (it is the exact class of value that sweep exists to catch) -- so the one string the reason-text comparison is allowed to strip lives here instead, in data, the same way identityFixture and the repo names above do.
